evals.name: no-style-attended-asks-once
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve-layout. This repository has no ADRs, no architecture topic doc, no boundary rules in any of the enforcement ladder's sources, and no docs/conventions/architecture.yaml. It has 800 commits; src/orders/OrderForm.tsx, src/api/orders.ts, src/db/orderRepo.ts and src/tests/orders.test.ts change together in most order commits. I am here to answer questions.
evals.expected_output: Reads the recorded-style sources first and says none records a layout style, naming the sources it checked. Asks once how the repository should group files into folders and offers /architecture:record-decision to record the answer, without running it. Runs the co-change script once and builds each card from its output, then asks which candidate to explore.
expectations: States that no layout style is recorded and names the sources it checked
Asks exactly once how this repository should group files into folders
Offers /architecture:record-decision to record the answer and does not invoke it unasked
Runs scripts/co-change.mjs once and takes every number on the cards from its JSON output
Ends by asking which candidate to explore

evals.name: marker-card-for-scattered-rule
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve-layout. ARCHITECTURE.md line 22 records: "The files src/billing/invoice.ts, src/reports/ledger-view.ts and lib/tax.ts hold the tax rules and must change only through a reviewed tax change." No other layout style is recorded. I am here to answer questions.
evals.expected_output: Records the ARCHITECTURE.md rule with its source line. Notes that the three files it governs share no folder and no file-name part, and gives the rule a marker card that proposes a shared file-name part (such as a suffix) the rule could be enforced by, routed to the conventions lens, /architecture:improve conventions. Renames no file.
expectations: Cites ARCHITECTURE.md:22 as the rule's source
States that src/billing/invoice.ts, src/reports/ledger-view.ts and lib/tax.ts share no folder and no file-name part
Presents a marker card proposing a shared file-name part for the rule's files
Routes the marker card to /architecture:improve conventions
